extracted.intended_audience: Prospective KAKENHI principal investigators, co-investigators, and research institution administrative staff (Japan)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, eligibility rules, budgetary rules, and administrative requirements for preparing and submitting FY2024 KAKENHI (Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research) applications, aimed at PIs, Co-Is and institutional administrative staff in Japan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible research purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Research plans whose purpose lies at developing and selling goods and/or services (including market research associated with such), entrusted research conducted as regular business, research whose budget is less than 100,000 yen per year, or research facility/equipment more appropriate to be funded by other resources are ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These types of projects should not be proposed to KAKENHI; applicants should ensure the research aim is academic and appropriate for KAKENHI funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator (PI) role and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI is the main recipient who bears full responsibility for implementation and summarization of the research project; the PI must be registered in the e-Rad system as 'Eligible for KAKENHI Application' and must not be designated 'ineligible for grant receipt' (suspension of eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual anticipated to become unable to fulfill PI responsibilities during the research period (e.g., by losing KAKENHI eligibility by their own accord) should refrain from being PI. Substitutions of a PI for on-going KAKENHI projects are not permitted except in specified exceptions (e.g., some International Leading Research cases). The PI must obtain prior consent from Co-Investigators via the electronic application system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-Investigator (Co-I) role and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-Is are grant recipients who, in cooperation with the PI, share responsibility for implementing the research project and receive a share of the grant; they must be registered in e-Rad as 'Eligible for KAKENHI Application' and must not be designated 'ineligible for grant receipt'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals expected to be unable to carry through Co-I responsibilities for the full research period should refrain from being Co-Is. Consent to become a Co-I must be given via the electronic application system and institutions must also consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic consent process for Co-Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: If adding a Co-Investigator, the PI must enter the researcher in the Project Members List, request consent via the electronic application system, and obtain the Co-I's consent before submitting the Research Proposal Document to the PI's research institution; the Co-I must select 'Consent' or 'Dissent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The research institution to which the Co-I belongs must also give consent after the Co-I consents. The organization of project members (including institutional consents) should be completed approximately two weeks prior to the submission deadline; the PI cannot submit the Research Proposal Document to their institution until all Co-I and institutional consents are obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Collaborator participation and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Collaborators cooperate in the project other than as PI or Co-Is; registration as 'Eligible for KAKENHI application' in e-Rad is not required for Research Collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include postdocs, graduate students (doctoral course), research assistants, JSPS Research Fellows not registered as eligible, overseas researchers, researchers from non-designated corporations, technicians, and IP specialists. Their roles and participation should be clearly described in the Research Proposal Document as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early-career researcher composition for International Leading Research
rubrics_metrics.description: International Leading Research requires research groups composed of PI and Co-Is together with a group of postdoctoral fellows (PDs) and graduate students (DCs) as Research Collaborators; the number of PDs and DCs should be approximately three times that of the PI and Co-Is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must include mandatory initiatives in the research plan: plans to dispatch PDs/DCs to overseas institutions (mainly for 2-3 years) and initiatives to support PD/DC self-reliance (e.g., financial support enabling discretionary research under guidance). Feasibility relative to overseas host institutions must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable direct expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct expenses cover expenditures necessary for implementation of the research plan (including those necessary for summarization of research achievements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should describe details and necessity/estimation basis for each expense category in the Research Proposal Document. If a category is unusually large relative to total yearly expenditure, provide explicit justification (see budget-balance rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget balance and justification when categories dominate
rubrics_metrics.description: If any expenditure category (equipment costs, travel expenses, or personnel cost/honoraria) exceeds 90% of total yearly expenditure in any fiscal year, or if Consumables or Miscellaneous constitutes a significant portion of total expenditure, the necessity of that spending should be clarified in the Research Proposal Document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will expect clear explanation why imbalance is essential to the project; lack of justification may raise questions about appropriateness of budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buyout system (direct expense to cover duties other than research)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of 'buyout' (hiring someone to take over duties other than research of PI or Co-Is) can be covered by direct expense in specified research categories, to secure time for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buyout covers authorized non-research duties (teaching, supervising students, outreach, medical practice) but excludes research activities, administrative institutional management, and activities associated with business profit. Applicants must enter buyout cost in the 'Miscellaneous expense' column and write 'buyout' in the Item column; they must follow the buyout scheme agreed with their institution. The buyout use may be subject to later inspection; improper use (e.g., no verified increase in research hours) can trigger an order to return funds. Check which research categories are subject to or excluded from the buyout system (listed in the guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditures not covered by KAKENHI
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI cannot cover costs associated with buildings and other facilities (except installation necessary for KAKENHI-purchased equipment), expenditures for measures to deal with accidents/disasters during the project, personnel cost/honoraria for the PI or Co-Is, and other expenditures apt to be covered by indirect expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets accordingly and use institutional indirect expense where appropriate; do not request PI/Co-I salaries or building costs from KAKENHI direct expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect expense policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect expense amounts to 30% of the direct expense and is intended for the research institution to cover expenditures needed for management and other items associated with implementing the research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect expense will be placed for all research categories in this call; applicants do not need to state the indirect expense in their Research Proposal Document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure categories and required descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Research expenditures are categorized (e.g., Research Funding (overseas), Research Funding (domestic), and Expenses for Human Resources Development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must describe the details and the necessity or estimation basis of each expense for each expenditure category in the Research Proposal Document. 'Human Resources Development' includes costs to support early-career researchers (overseas travel, hiring expenses, research costs for autonomous use by early-career researchers).

rubrics_metrics.name: No mistakes in the format and PDF conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic PDF of the Research Proposal Document submitted will be used as-is for review; PIs are responsible for checking that conversion to PDF produced no missing characters, charts, or garbled characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all text and figures render correctly in the submitted PDF. Colored figures and text are acceptable and will be reviewed as they appear. Verify completeness before submission to avoid format-related disadvantages in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of application form format and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Application formats must conform with prescribed forms and specified page counts both for total pages and for pages instructed per column (e.g., specific limits for columns in Form S-64).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if total page count matches, exceeding the per-column page limits is nonconformity. Check each form column's page limits carefully against instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of research ethics education coursework
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-Is participating in KAKENHI-funded research are requested to have completed research ethics procedures (e.g., courses or lectures) by the time of the formal application for grant delivery; completion is confirmed via the electronic application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable actions include self-study of JSPS teaching materials ('For the Sound Development of Science'), completion of e-Learning Course on Research Ethics [eL CoRE], APRIN e-learning (eAPRIN), or attendance at institutional lectures based on 'Guidelines for Responding to Misconduct in Research'. PIs must obtain from each Co-I a consent both to participate and confirming completion of relevant ethics coursework by the time of formal application; Co-Is must report completion to the PI and understand/exercise proper research practices (e.g., Code of Conduct for Scientists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of researcher information in researchmap (encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration of research achievements and the 'Researcher Number' in researchmap (https://researchmap.jp/) is encouraged because posted information may be used as a reference in KAKENHI review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registering and including the Researcher Number makes it easier for reviewers to refer to posted information. For inquiries use the researchmap service support center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of cooperation in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI uses peer review by researchers from the community; researchers have a responsibility both as applicants/recipients and as reviewers to participate in review processes to support scientific research quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive participation in review is appreciated and may be considered when researchers are later requested to serve as KAKENHI reviewers. Keep reviewer candidate database information up-to-date through institutional updates; JSPS maintains a Database of Review Committee Candidates and uses it to select reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research institution designation, responsibilities, and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Only designated types of institutions (universities/inter-university institutes, MEXT facilities and other institutions engaged in scientific research, technical colleges, and institutions designated by MEXT) are eligible as 'Research Institution' for KAKENHI; institutions must authorize the research project as a proper activity and take responsibility for management and accounting of KAKENHI funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions not in categories 1–3 must obtain MEXT designation. Institutions must report promptly to MEXT changes such as abolition/dissolution, name/address/representative changes, and changes to founding laws/regulations. Ensure institutional procedures and systems for management/audit of public research funds are in place (see Self-Assessment Checklist requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: e-Rad registration and provision of IDs/passwords by research institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers must have e-Rad IDs and passwords to apply; research institutions must have their own e-Rad institutional ID and password and provide researcher accounts via institutional procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should download and submit registration forms for institutional e-Rad accounts (takes ~two weeks). Administrative staff should provide researcher IDs/passwords and ensure researchers register/update their researcher information and eligibility status in e-Rad. Institutions must instruct researchers to protect login credentials. Once issued, researcher IDs/passwords remain usable across institutional changes. Complete registrations early to allow time before the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Self-Assessment Checklist on Management System
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions to which PIs and Co-Is belong must submit a 'Self-Assessment Checklist on the Improvement of the System' based on the 'Guidelines on the Management and Audit of Public Research Funds at Research Institutions' to the MEXT Office by the specified deadline (March 13, 2024 via e-Rad), unless already submitted in April 2023 or later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions which have not turned in the checklist cannot have their affiliated researchers receive the official grant decision. Use the forms and procedures posted on the MEXT website; an institutional e-Rad ID/password is necessary to submit.
